name: Ta Hien beer corner
kicker: Bia hoi corner at Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen
summary: After dark, Ta Hien is where the Old Quarter sits down for a beer: low tables and blue plastic stools pushed out across the street, grills and menu boards along the shopfronts, and the crowd shuffling between them. Order bia hoi, Hanoi’s fresh draft beer, at the corner with Luong Ngoc Quyen. Come after dinner, not in the daytime, when the street is quiet.
getThere: Walk the lanes north of Hoan Kiem Lake
heroCaption: Ta Hien at night, the street filled with stools, tables, and people
body: The corner of Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen is the bia hoi corner of the Old Quarter. Once it is dark the bars and kitchens set low tables and plastic stools across the pavement and into the road, and the lane becomes one long terrace.

Bia hoi is Hanoi’s fresh draft beer, unpasteurized and drunk soon after it is made, and sitting on a sidewalk stool with a glass of it is a local habit. Take a stool, order a glass, and watch the lane go past.
By day the same street is quiet: lanterns, shutters, and a few bicycles on the wet paving. Come back after dinner for the corner.

figures.caption: Ta Hien by day, red lanterns over the quiet lane
figures.alt: A narrow Old Quarter street in daylight, red lanterns on the left and bars with shutters on the right

gettingThere: Ta Hien is in the lanes north of Hoan Kiem Lake. Walk north from the lake into the quarter and follow the noise to the corner with Luong Ngoc Quyen.

legs.heading: From Hoan Kiem Lake
legs.body: On foot, north into the lanes to the corner of Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen.

hours: The Old Quarter is open 7am to midnight (Vietnam Tourism). Bar and kitchen hours: Check on arrival.
admissionNote: No entry fee for the street. Drink prices: Check on arrival.
